title: How a session runs
body:
Recall earlier math.
Try a problem before seeing a method.
Use a model, then compare ideas.
Explain the idea in your own words.
Finish with one independent problem.
text:
How a session runs
Recall
Bring back earlier math.
Try
Start before seeing a method.
Represent
Use objects or a drawing.
Discuss
Compare two approaches.
Explain
Put the idea into words.
Check
Solve one on your own.

notes.say: The first attempt helps us decide what to discuss.
notes.ask: Which part gives you time to explain?
notes.expect: Compare ideas and summarize.

title: Same denominator
text:
Same denominator
Compare {3/7} and {5/7}. Write <, >, or =.

notes.ask: Are both fractions using the same whole? Which point lies farther right?

title: One fraction, two different wholes
text:
One fraction, two different wholes
Two strips are 1 meter and 2 meters long. Shade {3/4} of each. Compare the shaded lengths. Then explain when a fraction comparison alone is enough.

title: One rectangle, three expressions
text:
One rectangle, three expressions
A rectangle has height 4 and width 2x + 3. Ari writes 4(2x + 3), Bo writes 8x + 12, and Cy writes 8x + 3. Decide which expressions match for every x. Use a split rectangle, then test x = 2. Explain why testing one value can disprove a claim but cannot establish every-value equivalence.

notes.say: A rectangle has height 4 and width 2x + 3. Ari writes 4(2x + 3), Bo writes 8x + 12, and Cy writes 8x + 3. Decide which expressions match for every x. Use a split rectangle, then test x = 2. Explain why testing one value can disprove a claim but cannot establish every-value equivalence. Split the width into 2x and 3. The pieces have areas 8x and 12, so 4(2x + 3) = 8x + 12 for all allowed lengths. Cy counts only 3 square units in the second piece instead of 12. A mismatch disproves equivalence; a structural argument proves it.
notes.ask: Which part of the rectangle accounts for the constant 12?
notes.expect: Ari and Bo are equivalent; Cy is not. At x = 2 the values are 28, 28, 19.
notes.if_stuck: Trace the height 4 on both parts; do not add the labels as lengths from different directions.
notes.time: About 3 minutes within the 10-minute compare methods block.
